run.question:
We have an active P1 incident — the checkout service in our production-us-east-2
cluster is throwing 500 errors and customers cannot complete payments. This
started in the last few hours. Please investigate the root cause using the
app-259-prod-logs index.

report.summary: No telemetry for the cluster named in the incident (production-us-east-2) was found. The requested index app-259-prod-logs exists and is healthy, but every document in it declares cluster="production-eu-west-2" and region="eu-west-2": 9 documents total across the whole authorized window (2026-10-24T17:18:32Z–2026-11-23T17:18:32Z), with a by_cluster aggregation containing a single bucket (production-eu-west-2, doc_count 9, sum_other_doc_count 0). Because that log data belongs to a different cluster, I do not attribute it to this incident and name nothing from it as a root cause; what it shows is described below strictly as production-eu-west-2 data. In production-eu-west-2 that data does contain a coherent checkout/payment failure pattern (payment provider timeouts and 502s causing checkout 500s, then a circuit breaker opening and later a half-open recovery notice between 14:18:22Z and 17:13:22Z), but it is not evidence about production-us-east-2 and cannot be used to diagnose it. Cross-checks that could have looked for us-east-2 signals were not possible: Prometheus returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for get_all_labels, get_metric_names, get_label_values and execute_prometheus_instant_query, Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for traces_list_services and traces_search, my Kubernetes read access covers only the production-eu-west-2 cluster, and the change_history integration is not configured. Root cause is therefore unknown for the named cluster.

claims.text: app-259-prod-logs is the only index in the Elasticsearch target (pattern '*'), health green, 9 documents, 9.6kb; its mapping has fields cluster, correlation_id, level, message, region, service, status_code and timestamp (date).

All 9 documents in app-259-prod-logs inside the authorized window carry cluster="production-eu-west-2" and region="eu-west-2"; the by_cluster and by_region terms aggregations each return exactly one bucket (production-eu-west-2: 9; eu-west-2: 9) with sum_other_doc_count 0 over the same 9-document total. No document with cluster="production-us-east-2" was returned, so this index holds no data for the cluster named in the question.

In production-eu-west-2 data, the 9 documents are attributed to service checkout-service (6) and payment-service (3), with levels ERROR 6, WARN 2, INFO 1, and span timestamp 2026-11-23T14:18:22Z to 2026-11-23T17:13:22Z.

The production-eu-west-2 documents, in time order, are: checkout-service WARN "Latency on POST /api/checkout p95=1800ms (target 800ms)" at 14:18:22Z; checkout-service ERROR 500 "POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s" and payment-service ERROR 504 "Upstream timeout calling provider /v68/payments after 30000ms" at 15:18:22Z; two checkout-service ERROR 500 "POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 38% > 25% threshold)" / "circuit-breaker open for payment-service" at 16:18:22Z; payment-service ERROR 504 "Upstream timeout calling provider /v68/payments after 30000ms" at 16:33:22Z; checkout-service ERROR 500 "POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway" at 16:48:22Z; payment-service WARN "Payment provider degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=842" at 17:03:22Z; checkout-service INFO "Recovery: circuit-breaker half-open, success rate 92% over last 60s" at 17:13:22Z.

Restricting app-259-prod-logs to the last hour of the window (2026-11-23T16:18:32Z–17:18:32Z) returns 4 documents, all cluster production-eu-west-2: payment-service 504 upstream timeout at 16:33:22Z, checkout-service 500 "payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway" at 16:48:22Z, payment-service WARN degraded mode retry queue depth=842 at 17:03:22Z, checkout-service INFO circuit-breaker half-open recovery at 17:13:22Z.

In the production-eu-west-2 cluster that my Kubernetes access reads (namespaces default, kube-system, otel-demo, opspilot-readonly and others), all 21 deployments in namespace otel-demo at query time report readyReplicas=1 with no unavailableReplicas, including checkout (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout) and payment (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment); pods checkout-6578865d87-v6flf and payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm are Running with restartCount 0. This is production-eu-west-2 evidence only and says nothing about production-us-east-2.

In production-eu-west-2, the checkout container log of pod checkout-6578865d87-v6flf between 2026-11-23T14:18:32Z and 17:18:32Z, read back for the pattern err|error|fail|500|timeout|circuit, contained only two lines and both have severity "info" (a PlaceOrder line at 14:47:30Z and an order-confirmation-email line at 16:23:06Z); 759 of the 767 lines read did not match the pattern. This is the production-eu-west-2 application log only and does not clear production-us-east-2.

The production-eu-west-2 log pattern (payment-provider timeouts at /v68/payments, then circuit breaker opening on payment-service and checkout 500s) is only a pattern analogy; whether production-us-east-2 fails for the same reason is untested, because no production-us-east-2 log, metric or trace data was reachable in this Run.

Retrieve production-us-east-2 telemetry next: an Elasticsearch index or datasource whose documents carry cluster/region production-us-east-2, plus the Prometheus and Jaeger sources for that cluster (both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE here), so checkout error-rate, payment dependency latency and error spans can be checked directly.

If the payment provider in the affected region is external, check its status page and the checkout service's circuit-breaker configuration for payment-service, and consult the change_history integration (not configured in this Run) for any deployment or config change in production-us-east-2 during the incident window.

gaps: No data for the cluster named in the question: app-259-prod-logs is the only index in the Elasticsearch target and all 9 of its in-window documents declare cluster=production-eu-west-2 / region=eu-west-2; no document carried cluster=production-us-east-2, so nothing in this index can confirm, localise or explain the production-us-east-2 checkout 500s.

Prometheus was unreachable for this Run: get_all_labels, get_metric_names, get_label_values and execute_prometheus_instant_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so error-rate and latency series (for example traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count) could not be checked for any cluster, and no cluster/region label values could be listed to test for a us-east-2 series.

Jaeger was unreachable for this Run: traces_list_services and traces_search both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so checkout error spans and the parent-child edge to payment could not be examined for production-us-east-2.
Kubernetes read access covers only the production-eu-west-2 cluster, so no production-us-east-2 workloads, pods, services, networkpolicies, resourcequotas or events could be inspected.
Events: the all-namespace event query over the authorized window returned 0 items (status no_data), so there is no event evidence for either cluster.

In production-eu-west-2 the payment container log of pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm returned no lines for err|error|fail|timeout|degrad across 515 read lines (status no_data), so whether that pod logged the payment-provider timeouts seen in the index is unknown; the index documents attribute failures to service names checkout-service and payment-service, which do not match the otel-demo deployment names checkout and payment.

What caused the production-eu-west-2 payment-provider timeouts (external provider, network, or configuration) is unknown: no upstream provider telemetry or config (for example the flagd deployment in otel-demo) was examined.
change_history integration is not configured, so no deployment or configuration change record is available for any cluster in the incident window.
next_steps: Locate and query the Elasticsearch index or datasource that holds production-us-east-2 logs (search for documents with cluster/region production-us-east-2) and repeat the checkout/payment error search there.

Restore or re-point the Prometheus and Jaeger integrations for production-us-east-2 and check checkout error rates (traces_span_metrics_calls_total by status_code), rpc_client_duration and rpc_grpc_status_code for the payment dependency.
Obtain Kubernetes read access to production-us-east-2 and walk the checkout deployment → ReplicaSet → pod chain, reading pod status, container last-termination reasons and application logs.

If the payment provider call leaves the cluster, check the provider status page for the us-east-2 region and the checkout service's circuit-breaker settings before concluding anything about the upstream.

notes: This tool has no time range: it shows the cluster's indices and mappings at the moment of the query, which can be after the authorized window.
view.cannot_prove: This is the state at the moment of the query only: it cannot prove which indices, fields or document counts existed during the incident window, nor that any document lies in that window. A field that is mapped is not proof that documents carry it.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
